methodology.warmup: one untimed invocation of each operation before the measured loop
methodology.sql_counting: SQLAlchemy before_cursor_execute listener: counts cursor execute() calls (executemany batches counted once, flagged separately) and classifies each statement as SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; COMMIT is not counted
methodology.dml_row_counting: Two independent signals: (1) after_cursor_execute cursor.rowcount for INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE (rows affected, portable DBAPI evidence); (2) Session.before_flush counting of pending ScanIssueRecord instances inserted/deleted by the ORM unit of work. Progress publish amplification is reported from these measured events, not from hardcoded arithmetic.
methodology.orm_row_counting: InstanceEvents.load listeners on the ScanRun and ScanIssueRecord mapped classes: counts ORM instances materialized from database rows (lazy and eager loads alike).
methodology.index_caveat: Migration f075 adds composite indexes via Alembic, NOT via Base.metadata, so this harness's SQLite create_all database does not contain them. Index performance is a PostgreSQL artifact and is not measured here; statement/row counts and shapes are the portable evidence.
methodology.percentile_method: linear interpolation between closest ranks (numpy/Excel PERCENTILE.INC)

operations.description: Saved scan list, first page of 10, unfiltered (GET /scans?limit=10)
operations.notes: COUNT(*) + page SELECT; for rows with empty scanned_page_urls the list adds one column-only issue-page-URL query for the whole page (constant, replaces the historical per-row lazy loads).

operations.description: Saved scan list, first page of 50, unfiltered (GET /scans?limit=50)
operations.notes: Same statements as limit=10 but returns 50 scan rows; fallback URL resolution stays constant.

operations.description: Saved scan list, limit 10, status='complete' filter
operations.notes: Complete rows have scanned_page_urls populated, so no fallback query is issued. The (status, started_at) index from migration f075 is migration-only and therefore not present in this SQLite create_all database - the measured time is shape-only.

operations.description: Saved scan list, limit 10, q='site-42' (ILIKE on requested_url/final_url)
operations.notes: Two leading-wildcard ILIKE scans over requested_url/final_url; not indexable in PostgreSQL either.

operations.description: Saved scan detail for one scan with 100 issue rows (GET /scans/{id})
operations.notes: selectinload(ScanRun.issues): one SELECT for the run plus one SELECT ... WHERE scan_run_id IN (...).

Repository read with include_issues=False skips the selectinload query entirely; the response keeps its shape with issues=[]. This mirrors the API polling path measured by the backend owner (status/summary polling while a scan runs).

operations.description: Crawl-memory lookup called once per multi-page scan request (all complete scans of the user)
operations.notes: Identical scenario to the baseline. The implementation now selects only the URL-bearing columns (no issue eager-load); compare the measured SQL statement count and ORM rows loaded against the baseline's 2 SELECTs / 20,200 ORM rows.

operations.description: Worker queue refresh between pages (queued_page_urls + excluded_page_urls)
operations.notes: Called by CrawlQueueControl.refresh from the worker loop around every crawled page.

operations.description: Worker cancellation poll before/after every crawled page
operations.notes: Single SELECT of cancel_requested_at/status; called at least once per page.

operations.description: Worker claims the next queued job
operations.notes: SELECT ... WHERE status='queued' ORDER BY started_at LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + state UPDATE + refresh.

operations.description: Worker startup stale-job recovery over 20 stale running rows
operations.notes: One SELECT of stale runs + 20 row updates (one batched executemany) + commit.

operations.description: Persist a completed single-page scan result with 100 issues (worker completion path)
operations.notes: _replace_scan_issue_records: delete previous issue rows + insert 100 new rows + update summary counts + commit.

operations.description: Save a completed background single-page scan with 100 issues (in-request save path)
operations.notes: INSERT scan run + INSERT 100 issue rows + commit + refresh.

notes: Saved-scan list pages are resolved with a constant number of statements: limit=50 issued 3 SQL statements and the status-filtered page issued 2 (baseline: 45 vs 2; the historical per-row lazy-load N+1 is replaced by one batched column-only issue-page-URL query).

get_previously_scanned_page_urls_for_domain issued 1 SELECT(s) and materialized 0 ORM rows (baseline: 2 SELECTs / 20,200 ORM rows). The implementation selects requested_url/final_url/scanned_page_urls only.
get_saved_scan with 100 issues issued 2 SELECTs and materialized 101 ORM rows via selectinload (unchanged by design: the full detail response still needs the issues).
get_saved_scan_status_only (include_issues=False) issued 1 statement(s) and materialized 1 ORM rows, confirming the polling read never touches issue rows.

progress_write_amplification.description: Worker publish cycle: update_scan_progress called once per crawled page with cumulative issue lists 100->200->300->400->500 (5 publishes per iteration)

measured_write_amplification.measurement_method: Measured from SQLAlchemy after_cursor_execute cursor.rowcount (DML rows) and Session.before_flush ORM instance counts; not hardcoded arithmetic. A delete performed via a bulk query before the timed loop is not part of the cycle.

progress_write_amplification.notes: update_scan_progress now appends only issues that are not persisted yet (count/max-position SELECT, then insert the tail), so the measured row-event totals above show the real write amplification of the 5-page crawl. Completion still performs one authoritative replace.

limitations: SQLite in memory is not PostgreSQL: no network round-trip, no WAL/fsync, no planner statistics, no row locks (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED is ignored by SQLite). Absolute timings are optimistic lower bounds.

Migration f075 composite indexes are migration-only (not in Base.metadata), so this SQLite create_all database has none of them; index speed-ups are a PostgreSQL-only effect and are NOT measured by this harness. Statement/row counts are the portable evidence.
The database runs in the same process: PostgreSQL cost would add protocol serialization and network latency per statement.

Synthetic rows use uniform 100-issue scans; real scans vary widely, and single-page production saves can additionally carry large base64 screenshot data URLs in scan_issues.screenshot_data_url (not seeded here because the multi-page worker publish path does not capture screenshots).
No concurrent users or workers were simulated; contention, lock waits and connection-pool effects are out of scope for this benchmark.
